steps.name: 'Pencil Stub'
steps.text: Yeremey! You're still drinking? I had to turn the chemical factory upside down to find that single crate of beer!

steps.name: Yeremey
steps.text: Get lost—

steps.name: Nika
steps.text: Heh, let him drink, he's had plenty of scares these past few days.

steps.name: Yeremey
steps.text: Well *hic*... I pulled through *hic*... lousy beer *hic*... totally beneath me *hic*...

steps.name: 'Pencil Stub'
steps.text: O noble lord, what has brought you down so low, that you must beg a humble 'peasant' like me for drink?

steps.name: Yeremey
steps.text: No, you're a decent fellow *hic*... the best *hic*...

steps.name: Nika
steps.text: I'm a 'peasant' too, Yeremey, compliment me!

steps.name: Yeremey
steps.text: Forget it—*hic*!

steps.name: 'Pencil Stub'
steps.text: How did we get onto this topic? It's kind of embarrassing, really.

steps.name: Yeremey
steps.text: Listen, friends, I'll buy you a crate of beer for every cup I drink here.

steps.name: Yeremey
steps.text: Sonya, Mykola, Fedya, there'll be plenty for everyone!

steps.name: Nika
steps.text: You alright, Yeremey?

steps.name: 'Pencil Stub'
steps.text: Judging from the way he's chugging one beer after another, I'd say he's perfectly alright.

steps.name: 'Pencil Stub'
steps.text: How about you save the rest of the beer for us right now, because Fedya is sitting right behind you!

steps.name: Yeremey
steps.text: Not *hic* Not tonight... after tonight, whatever you want *hic*—

steps.name: Botani
steps.text: Why don't you sit with the others?

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: What about you, the conquering hero who captured the enemy?

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: Sonya and Antosha have been interrogating him all day. We should know more soon.

steps.name: Botani
steps.text: Let's hope it'll bring about the end of Gromov's tyranny...

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: You don't sound happy.

steps.name: Botani
steps.text: I've been thinking about what caused the radio blackout in the quarantine zone.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: The Third Bureau has its ways.

steps.name: Botani
steps.text: But your equipment still caught my signal. How...?

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: You ask too many questions, 'Botani'... 'bookworm', indeed.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: There aren't many earnest folk in Ursus these days... I can't believe I've become so nostalgic.

steps.name: Botani
steps.text: ...I know you're hiding something from us, Fedya.

steps.name: Botani
steps.text: If you don't want to talk about it, I'll just pretend not to notice.

steps.name: Botani
steps.text: But I couldn't have brought Baron Pavalo back without you... you're the true hero on that front.

steps.name: Botani
steps.text: Maybe one day, you'll be a hero to even more people...

steps.name: 'Pencil Stub'
steps.text: Fedya! Botani! Want a drink?

steps.name: 'Pencil Stub'
steps.text: Yeremey sure is strong when he's drunk. He won't let me near the booze.

steps.name: 'Pencil Stub'
steps.text: Well, he's finally out cold now, and I punched him a couple of times for good measure. He's not waking up for a while.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: 'Pencil Stub'
steps.text: Anyway, we've got enough for four cups. Want to sit down and chat a little? I'd love to make friends...

steps.name: Botani
steps.text: Sure, Pencil Stub. I think this is the first time you've seen my face?

steps.name: 'Pencil Stub'
steps.text: Hah, you scared people when you showed up covered in blood, but we all relaxed when we heard your voice.

steps.name: Nika
steps.text: Anyway, I've got your cups. This one's for you, Fedya.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: ...Spasibo.

steps.name: 'Pencil Stub'
steps.text: To tomorrow!

steps.name: Nika
steps.text: To victory!

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: To...

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: To souls happy and free.

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: ...I cannot accept this compromise.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Unless you got a better idea. You can torture him if you want, but the only thing he cares about is his own hide.

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: I warned you, Pavalo is the prototypical Ursine noble.

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: Short-sighted, cowardly, ever dreaming of kindness and 'guidance' from above, acting harmless while pocketing all the gold and silver.

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: Give them a chance to catch their breath, and they will not hesitate to draw their swords against the people, and offer bloodshed to their liege lords as a gift.

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: Walking corpses whose expertise is self-preservation... can you not smell their stench?

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: We can keep arguing, or we can spend our time making more urgent plans. The intel I extracted from him includes a map of the Sixteen Warriors headquarters.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: They've got lots of supplies there, and he says Gromov has been gone a lot lately. This is the perfect opportunity.

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: He will sell you out, if he gets out alive... you'll have every policeman in Ursus on your tail, even if you manage to get out of Katorga. Do we really want to meet again in court?

spans.text: sell you out, if he gets out alive... you'll have every policeman in Ursus on your tail, even if you manage to get out of Katorga. Do we really want to meet again in court?

steps.name: Matvey
steps.text: At least we share the common goal of liberating this raion right now. We can argue about the rest later.

steps.name: Matvey
steps.text: Assaulting their headquarters is no easy task. We are willing to work with you, but we'll need to rest and regroup. Perhaps—

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Understood. Once we are all set, we will move out and have Pavlo lead the way.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: What do you think, Antosha?

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: Bring plenty of guys, Sonya. Do not underestimate him.

steps.name: Botani
steps.text: ...Sonya?

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Shh. I don't want to wake them up.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: I just wanted to... get some rest by the fire.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: You've done a huge service for the people here. But I'm still not sure if I'm a leader worthy of any of that.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: When I got back to Ursus, I thought about living a normal life back home, but all of us are still struggling in the mud, me and all the girls who follow me...

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: I've let a lot of people down, watched my friends die... soon, I'll be leading them on another journey.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Can we go back to our old lives? Or am I just gonna fail at everything...?

steps.name: Botani
steps.text: You've already achieved a lot, haven't you?

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: ...Huh?

steps.name: Botani
steps.text: You can have half my beer. I haven't touched it yet.
Zima reflexively takes the cup and inhales the faint scent of wheat, while faint snoring rings in her ears.
She scans the peaceful sleeping faces, red and puffy, smacking their lips in their dreams... it is the most peaceful night they have had since they came to the quarantine zone.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Hm...

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Half a cup, even if it's just half a cup...

steps.name: 'Sixteen Warriors' Guard
steps.text: Boss, take it easy.

steps.name: Gromov
steps.text: Where is Pavlovich? Spit it out!

steps.name: Gromov
steps.text: Why did those mudaki take my cannons? Why did they cut the supplies? I want an explanation!

spans.text: take my cannons? Why did they cut the supplies? I want an explanation!

steps.name: 'Sixteen Warriors' Guard
steps.text: The magistrate will be back soon. I'm sure it'll all sort itself out.

steps.name: 'Sixteen Warriors' Guard
steps.text: He gave us money, and those bodyguards he has—

steps.name: Gromov
steps.text: Blyat! I don't need you to tell me that! Pizdets!

spans.text: I don't need you to tell me that!

steps.text: He picks up a chair and throws it into a corner, then hears a frail, frightened chirping.

steps.name: Gromov
steps.text: ...What's that?
Gromov lifts the velvet covering the box, revealing an elaborate cage and its resident, a brown beckbeast trembling in a corner.

steps.name: Gromov
steps.text: Pavlovich's? He didn't take his stupid pet with him today...

steps.name: Gromov
steps.text: You, wait outside.

steps.name: 'Sixteen Warriors' Guard
steps.text: Yes sir!
After his subordinate has left, Gromov grins, He will bring his arrogant employer down a peg.
Rough hands reach into the cage, put themselves around the poor little creature's neck, and twist...

steps.name: Pavlovich
steps.text: Gromov! I didn't expect to see you here. I heard you were looking for me?

steps.name: Pavlovich
steps.text: ...Why are you staring at my beckbeast like that?

steps.name: Gromov
steps.text: What is it doing here...?

steps.name: Pavlovich
steps.text: We don't see each other for a few days, and you've already forgotten? How could I go without its companionship?

steps.name: Gromov
steps.text: Uh...

steps.name: Pavlovich
steps.text: Feeling jealous? Hah, I knew you loved small animals too.

steps.name: Pavlovich
steps.text: There's another one in my office that's going to breed with this one. You can have one of the babies.

steps.name: Security Team Captain
steps.text: Where's your gratitude?

steps.name: Pavlovich
steps.text: Don't worry about it.

steps.name: Pavlovich
steps.text: I don't suppose you came for this. What has you in such a hurry?
Gromov takes one look at the bodyguards, all of them bigger than him, and swallows the profanities that he had intended to say.

steps.name: Gromov
steps.text: Why did you cut our supplies, sir? We're having enough trouble handling those kids as it is.

steps.name: Pavlovich
steps.text: Do you remember why I hired you to manage Katorga Raion, Gromov? You were the lowest bidder.

steps.name: Pavlovich
steps.text: I hope you have not forgotten this excellent quality.

steps.name: Gromov
steps.text: Then my cannons—

steps.name: Pavlovich
steps.text: Do not mention them again. I wouldn't tell you, even if I knew.

steps.name: Pavlovich
steps.text: This is noble business. Do your job!

steps.name: 'Sixteen Warriors' Ruffian
steps.text: Boss! We've got a problem!

steps.name: Gromov
steps.text: What?

steps.name: 'Sixteen Warriors' Ruffian
steps.text: Th-The students found the 'Honor Room'!

steps.name: Gromov
steps.text: Blyat! How's that possible?!

steps.name: 'Sixteen Warriors' Ruffian
steps.text: I just came from there! Sonya is gonna get in, if we don't send help!

steps.name: Gromov
steps.text: Magistrate!

steps.name: Pavlovich
steps.text: Assign half our security team to him.

steps.name: Security Team Captain
steps.text: Yes sir!

steps.name: Pavlovich
steps.text: If anything goes wrong, I will feed your pieces to my beckbeast. You understand?

steps.name: Pavlovich
steps.text: Now get lost!

steps.name: 'Pencil Stub'
steps.text: ...Exterior is clear. Cleaning up.

steps.name: 'Pencil Stub'
steps.text: These guys can fight, but they have absolutely no discipline.

steps.name: Yeremey
steps.text: Are things going well on the General's side? She should be inside their HQ by now.

steps.name: Nika
steps.text: The Sixteen Warriors will fight tooth and nail to protect it. We need to get over there and back them up, fast.

steps.name: 'Pencil Stub'
steps.text: Let's hope Gromov has some real food here. I've had enough of cans—
His smile freezes on his face. He sways and falls by the feet of his friends. There is a crossbow bolt straight through his chest.
Yeremey's eyes widen. He sees Gromov approach with a dozen massive brutes in tow.

steps.name: Nika
steps.text: Hurry! Stop them!

steps.name: Gromov
steps.text: Blyat!

steps.name: Gromov
steps.text: Die, mudak!

steps.name: Yeremey
steps.text: No!
Yeremey's steel pipe meets Yeremey's hamaxe, and he is sent flying like a balloon.

steps.name: Nika
steps.text: Yeremey! No!

steps.name: Gromov
steps.text: Your turn, cherv.

steps.name: Nika
steps.text: Gromov...!

steps.name: Nika
steps.text: You will pay for your crimes, murderer!

steps.name: Nika
steps.text: I'll kill you or die trying!
Blood rushes up her throat, and she can speak no more.
With great effort, Nika turns her neck to look in Yeremey's direction. She sees her friends scrambling to form a line, while Gromov has already charged inside like a monster.
I knew it was a trap the moment you said you were going to bribe Gromov and get him to let us out.
But why did I go with you... Yeremey?

steps.name: Gromov
steps.text: Govno, govno, govno!

steps.name: Gromov
steps.text: It's not over yet... We can cut through the back—it's faster. My men must still be fighting inside.

steps.name: Gromov
steps.text: I'm the only one who knows the passphrase to the Honor Room. I'll hand out the weapons inside and turn this around...

steps.name: Gromov
steps.text: The door's just ahead—

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: I got the last one, General!

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: ...Gromov?!
A brief silence, then Gromov leaps towards a machine on the wall.

steps.name: Authentication Device
steps.text: Please speak the passphrase.

steps.name: Gromov
steps.text: *Expletives*!

steps.name: Authentication Device
steps.text: Passphrase incorrect.

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: Watch out! That button must be hiding something!

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: Matvey!
The bolt hits Gromov's left arm. He roars and manages to fend off his attackers by swinging his hamaxe.

steps.name: Authentication Device
steps.text: Please speak the passphrase.

steps.name: Gromov
steps.text: *Expletives*!

steps.name: Authentication Device
steps.text: Passphrase incorrect.

steps.name: Gromov
steps.text: *Ursine roar*!

steps.name: Authentication Device
steps.text: Passphrase correct.

steps.name: Authentication Device
steps.text: Welcome, brave Gromov, descendant of Igor Velikiy's sixteen bravest companions...

steps.name: Authentication Device
steps.text: He whose will is unbreakable, heir to the unstoppable legendary hamaxe...
Before the recording can finish, Gromov has already charged through the facade, using the momentum to roll inside.
Leto's strike misses, destroying the annoying box instead.

steps.name: Authentication Device
steps.text: *Bzz*... the Sixteen Warriors... usher... next golden age of Ursus!

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Who d'you think you are?!
Gromov tries to reach out, but a crossbow bolt hits the wall in front of him, just an inch from his finger.

steps.name: Gromov
steps.text: I recognize you, and you... the Unbound.
He jumps back and punches a brick on the wall, causing two transparent 'walls' to drop down between Gromov and the others.

steps.name: Gromov
steps.text: I originally designed this 'prison' for Pavlovich. I never thought I'd be its first prisoner.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Did you think a single pane of glass would—
Zima punches the glass, only to be knocked back several steps.

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Something's funny about this glass!

steps.name: Gromov
steps.text: The Third Bureau's shiny new toy, a new type of material that not even the tsar has seen... makes you wonder, doesn't it? Who did they make it for?

steps.name: Gromov
steps.text: Better find yourself a landship if you want to break it... haha!
Gromov sits down on the floor, panting, but relaxed enough to begin tying his shoelaces.

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: We don't have much time... reinforcements will be here any moment. The guys outside can't hold for long.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: There must be a way!

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: The Sixteen Warriors... wait a minute!

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Why are there two of the same hamaxes here in this room?
The sixteen heroes who fought alongside Igor Velikiy were the bravest and strongest warriors of their time...
The street thugs who took their name forged a hamaxe in imitation of the legendary weapon, only to find themselves unworthy, lacking the strength to lift the glorious weapon.
Therefore, Gromov put the 'authentic' weapon on display, and carries a replica.

steps.name: Gromov
steps.text: You're crazy! No one can swing that thing!

steps.name: Gromov
steps.text: You'll only hurt yourself!

steps.name: Botani
steps.text: Sonya, do you need help—
Botani's jaw drops as she watches Sonya smash the display glass and raise the hamaxe into the air. She can almost hear Sonya's bones creak at the stress.
Zima slowly walks towards the impregnable glass wall, dragging the hamaxe behind her.

steps.name: Gromov
steps.text: No... no, no, no, no, no!

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Looks like I'm more worthy than you...

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Right?!

steps.name: Gromov
steps.text: No!

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: This is for all the people you murdered, all the evil you've allowed, the judgment and punishment that you've dodged all this time... this is for pissing me off.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Any last words, Gromov?

steps.name: Gromov
steps.text: How—How could you possibly lift it—
The words have hardly left his mouth before Zima brings the hamaxe down. In the brief moment that it takes to find its mark, Zima seems to feel it grow lighter in her hand.
No longer the stuff of legend, nor an artifact that should sit in a museum collecting dust, and certainly not the plaything of a murderer—
It is power.
The power to resist, to sweep aside obstacles, to cut open the path of life.
It has no opinion, no position, no intention, no emotion.
It is life's primal roar, the first drop of blood that the heart pumps with each beat. It ignores all the complicated things in this world. All it does is—

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Fight!!!

steps.name: Tired Student
steps.text: Sonya... we're saved.

steps.name: Tired Student
steps.text: The thugs ran for the upper walls once they saw Gromov's remains.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Good work... I know everyone fought bravely.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Do a head count, take as many supplies as you can, and the fallen—

steps.name: Pavalo
steps.text: Sonya! Sonya! Over here!

steps.name: Pavalo
steps.text: Keep your people in check!

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: She can't stop me. No one can.

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: Your Well Born death will make Ursus a better place, Baron.

steps.name: Pavalo
steps.text: What are you saying—help me!

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Calm down, Antosha!

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: ...We had a deal, Antosha.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: He gives us the location, we spare his life.

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: I told you, Sonya, I will not suffer any of these leeches to live. Whatever value they might offer can only extend their lives for a few hours.

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: Allow them to live, and it will be our friends who die. It will be the workers in the mines, the farmers in the wilderness.

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: At the moment of death, his pathetic life will offer its last worth, and atone for his sins.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: No. You're wrong.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: He only has value if he gets out alive. That'll tell the other opportunists like him that we can be reasoned with, that they can negotiate.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: The empire isn't one big thing, it never was. This is how we'll trip them up, exploit their differences, and get what we want as fast and easy as we can.

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: And my goal is to see all oppression gone from Ursus, from all of Terra.

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: I swore upon the future of this land that I will break its spine with my own hands and await a new dawn upon its ruins.

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: I do not kill these leeches for vengeance. I kill them so that this teetering house of cards will collapse more cleanly.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Killing a former noble who has already lost everything, begging for his life like a beckbeast...

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: You think a death like that means anything?

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: All I know is that this is a country where the freedom of the wealthy is built upon the corpses of the poor.

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: Every one of them we kill is a life saved.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: You're out to smash things, but you don't get that breaking stuff is just a means, not an end.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Rubble's not enough. We need unity. We need people, people who will stand with us and fight injustice when we need them most.

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: Really? Allowing a man like this to live is the greatest injustice to those he has exploited.

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: Enough, Sonya. Botani caught this man. It is your right to do with him as you please.

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: But, if you are willing to work with them, then this is where we part ways. The Unbound will work with you no longer.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Don't be stupid, Antosha!

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: You're burning bridges, hurting your own cause, and putting the people who follow you in danger!

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: The Unbound don't follow me. I am simply their advisor.

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: All of us have gathered here of our own volition, to act in every corner in Ursus where oppression exists, to help those who suffer fight back against the cruelty of the nobility.

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: Anyone is free to leave, if they don't agree with me. Anyone can remove me.
Antosha turns around to seek Matvey's gaze.
This is a habit that he developed when they left school together, whenever he says something, goes somewhere, or kills someone.
Matvey always casts a supporting gaze from behind, helping him affirm that he is sober, and walking the right path.
Even Ukusik knows that Matvey will tell Antosha when he goes wrong.
But now—
There is no one there.

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: There you are, Matvey.

steps.name: Matvey
steps.text: Yes.
Matvey is standing in the snow. He takes a bloody cigarette and puts it in his mouth, only to cough violently at the acrid smoke.

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: ...I never knew you smoked.

steps.name: Matvey
steps.text: I never knew you killed for the sake of killing.

steps.name: Matvey
steps.text: Some of them may be criminals who have yet to be judged. But they are not monsters doomed to be slain.

steps.name: Matvey
steps.text: You unleashed violence upon them, but allowed them to escape judgment... law and order have no place in your heart.

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: ...You've told me that dozens of times. But there's no better way to uphold justice for the ordinary man. Unless you—

steps.name: Matvey
steps.text: No, Antosha.

steps.name: Matvey
steps.text: You are an aristocrat, and an Ursine. Every time I saw you kill someone, I couldn't help but wonder if they were actually men, just like you.

steps.name: Matvey
steps.text: But you never gave anyone else the same opportunity you had.
Matvey puts the burning cigarette in the snow, with the others that have fallen upon the white, soaked and crushed beneath the heels of passersby.
Then he turns around, walking the path from whence he came.

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: ...I didn't kill Pavalo.
But Matvey is already far away.

steps.name: Ukusik
steps.text: Antosha... are you fighting with Matvey?

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: No. Don't ask questions like this.

steps.name: Ukusik
steps.text: Then... can I go and see Rosalind tonight? She told me she'd tell me stories about her time in Kjerag after we beat Gromov.

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: No, don't go there.

steps.name: Ukusik
steps.text: What about tomorrow?

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: Not tomorrow either, Ukusik. Don't go there anymore.

steps.name: Ukusik
steps.text: But aren't we gonna fight together to tear down that wall?

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: We will...

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: But Sonya has her path, and we have ours.

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: We will learn which is the right one.

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: At any price.

steps.name: Botani
steps.text: What are you doing, Fedya?

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: A head count, and preparing food for tomorrow.

steps.name: Botani
steps.text: Head count... how many did we lose?

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: At least several. Possibly dozens. Some are still being treated.

steps.name: Botani
steps.text: I was happy that I finally did something that was absolutely right... but in the end—

steps.name: Botani
steps.text: Things didn't seem to get better. We lost so many friends... and split with Antosha's group...

steps.name: Botani
steps.text: Did I really make things better for people, Fedya, like that voice from the Far North? Even just a little bit?

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: You mean that criminal wanted for illegal broadcasting?

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: ...Yes. You did the right thing.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: But I don't think you need me to judge what you've done.
Fyodor lights the campfire that has been out for a while.
He digs out a lonely potato lying in an ash heap, puts a wooden skewer through it, and begins to roast it.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: Because what really matters isn't what I say... but how you view yourself.

steps.name: Botani
steps.text: Should I consider that a lecture?

steps.name: Botani
steps.text: I don't know... maybe you're right. No. Maybe I'm right.

steps.name: Botani
steps.text: That night, we sat together by the fireside and roasted potatoes just like this.

steps.name: Botani
steps.text: That was the first time you joined the circle of students, chatting with them, talking politics, discussing literature...

steps.name: Botani
steps.text: That was the first time I saw with my own eyes the people I only knew by voice.

steps.name: Botani
steps.text: It was wonderful...

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: ...Your efforts were never futile.

steps.name: Botani
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Botani
steps.text: I was the voice on the headset. I think I'll continue to be that.

steps.name: Botani
steps.text: Thanks, Fedya!

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: 'That night, we sat together by the fireside and roasted potatoes just like this...'

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: Pencil Stub...

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: Yeremey...

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: Nika...

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: Shorty...

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: This is for you.
Fyodor's hands cannot stop trembling. The hands that gave the chervontsy to Shorty...
The hands that saved lives...
The hands that wrought countless deaths...
Fyodor cannot describe his feelings in words. He can feel his excitement, and genuine fear...
By the time Fyodor wakes from his reverie, the campfire has been reduced to a small lick of flame, trembling in the darkness.
One side of the potato is burnt, while the other side is still raw.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: 'Tomorrow will come'...

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: Such a simple prayer.
